transcript: The other night I saw Dark Noon at St Ann's Warehouse. I feel like every time I see something at St Ann's I'm always left thinking about something, but this piece unfortunately left me feeling a bit stranded. In this wildly theatrical retelling of American history, a small group of actors colonize the stage, bringing in set pieces and audience members along the way. American history is dark and violent and this production did not shy away from that. I think it's meant to be satirical but I mostly found it straight up horrifying. And the pieces of humour here and there felt tonally out of place for me. Although I was mesmerized by the stagecraft, and very impressed by the performances, I wasn't exactly sure what my takeaway was supposed to be at the end. And without this clear sense of direction, I felt it unfortunately dragged despite only being an hour and 45 with no intermission. The final portion of this play gives us some context around the group of actors themselves, and I found this to be perhaps the most interesting part of the entire piece. But still I didn't fully understand the connection with the rest of it in order to see it as a payoff, so to speak. Nonetheless, there was plenty about this piece to appreciate, and folks for the most part seemed into it. With that, another playbill for my collection.
